name: variable-font-and-cursor
title: Variable Font and Cursor
description: A single word whose thickness and slant follow the mouse across its container, with faint crosshair guides and a live x and y readout tracking the pointer.
use: A portfolio or agency headline wants an interactive typographic moment that rewards moving the pointer.
avoid: Essential copy, since it needs a pointer and thins the text until it nearly disappears at one end.
a11y: Purely pointer-driven, so keyboard users get no equivalent, and no reduced-motion preference is checked. (keyboard: no, labels: n-a, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: An orange lowercase word sits centred on a black full-bleed stage. Faint grey crosshair lines and a tiny orange dot follow the pointer, with a small monospaced x and y readout at the lower left.
behaves: As the pointer moves, the word's weight and slant interpolate between set limits, sliding from hairline to heavy and upright to italic. The crosshair lines and coordinates travel with the cursor.
customise: Children are the text; fontVariationMapping picks which axis each cursor direction drives and its range, and containerRef sets the tracking area. The variable font itself must be loaded elsewhere.
weight: light: One text node restyled on each animation frame; no canvas or heavy node count.
demo: The word stash! in orange, with live x and y coordinates beneath it
issues: At the lightest setting the word turns hairline and almost vanishes against the black stage.
polishWhy: Sharp variable type and a clear crosshair; the bare demo and near-invisible light end lower it.
